messages:
carmen: Heads-up — proposing a schema split for console analytics: move per-route quota attributes (quota_window, token_limit, tier_id) out of routes table into a dedicated quota_profiles table. Plan: dual-write for 2 weeks, backfill historical rows, enable read-adapter that prefers quota_profiles -> fallback to routes for compatibility. Asking for concerns/edge cases.

josh: :eyes: can you sketch the migration steps and risky spots? particularly worried about read latency impact and index blowup.

carmen: short sketch: 1) Create quota_profiles (route_id, profile_id, window, limit, created_at, tenant_id + indexes). 2) Start dual-write in API server behind flag. 3) Backfill existing routes into quota_profiles (batch job). 4) Flip console read to use read-adapter that queries quota_profiles and falls back to routes within 200ms. 5) Monitor telemetry and dashboards, then cutover reads and drop columns after 30 days.

nate: for backfill do we plan single big job or partitioned by tenant shards? we should avoid hot partitions. also need idempotent upserts.

carmen: partitioned by tenant_shard, throttle to keep p99 latency under 150ms for ingest. job will use UPSERT on (route_id) and track progress per shard. idempotency token included.

eva: what about the API fast-path that currently reads quota from the same hot route row? if read-adapter adds a second call to quota_profiles it could add 1 extra read per request. Can we co-locate or cache?

carmen: good point. plan: read-adapter will first try a local cache (in-process tiered LRU keyed by route_id + profile_etag). If cache miss, do single multi-get to storage using route_id->profile_id index. Also keep the fallback to route column for <30 days to avoid steady-state double read.

marie: console dashboards rely on telemetry counters that include quota config - moving table changes the telemetry pipeline. we'll need to update telemetry enrichment to join quota_profiles on route_id in ingest and re-run any compactification backfills for derived metrics.

carmen: yes — telemetry changes: add new join in enrichment, emit feature.quality events for profile mismatches during dual-write. We'll create a dashboard card: quota-profile-dualwrite-errors, backfill-progress, read-fallback-rate, adapter-latency.

josh: SQL snippet for DDL?

josh: ```sql
CREATE TABLE quota_profiles (
  route_id uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  profile_id uuid NOT NULL,
  window_seconds int NOT NULL,
  token_limit bigint NOT NULL,
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);
ALTER TABLE routes DROP COLUMN quota_window CASCADE; -- only after cutover
```

carmen: exact schema will include (tenant_shard, route_id) composite primary for scalability and a separate profiled_by_tenant index.

nate: rollback plan? if dual-write causes problems we need a safe revert.

carmen: revert path: flip flag to stop writing quota_profiles (writes go to routes only), keep read-adapter pointing to routes, cancel backfill or mark incomplete, and alert. we never drop columns until we're stable.

eva: can we add a canary rollout: enable dual-write for 5% tenants, watch dashboards for errors and read-fallback-rate?

carmen: yes — we'll do tenant-based canary: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h soak each. infra-bot will auto-roll back on >0.1% error budget breach.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: dual-write feature flag created: ff/quota_profiles_dualwrite. Canary pipeline ready. Monitor group: #ingest-alerts, #console-observability.

marie: timeline request from PMs: can we aim for first canary next Tuesday? need communication to support so they can expect glitches in console UX.

carmen: target: canary next Tue, broader ramp over 3 weeks. I'll draft runbook and post link.

josh: tests: unit + integration + chaos: simulate missing profile rows and high-latency storage. we should validate API p95 stays under 120ms.

carmen: agreed. I'll add integration tests to route-service test harness and a QA job that replays production traffic subset.

eva: small UX ask: console should surface when quota source is 'route' vs 'profile' during rollout so support can explain.

carmen: good call. we'll add a small badge in the Console: "quota source: legacy(route)/profiles" and make it filterable.

nate: one more: revise data retention policy for quota_profiles (TTL?) probably keep indefinitely but tie to tenant deletion.

carmen: keep until tenant deletion + soft-delete cascade. we'll document in storage-contracts.

marie: thanks — please post the runbook and the migration checklist when ready. :thumbsup:

carmen: will do. sending a draft later today. thanks everyone.
